brief: Daily GS marketcolour report covering Thursday's session recap, positioning data, an equity-strategy call, two stock calls, and a transport-sector chartpack. US equities closed higher (SPX +114bps to 7637, NDX +173bps, RTY +55bps), led by tech and consumer discretionary. Single-stock movers included GNRC (+18.3% on an Amazon data-center generator deal) and FLNC (-15.4% on a FY26 revenue cut). PB data showed L/S gross leverage at 208.8% and net leverage at 48.8%. Asset managers and hedge funds were both net buyers, and CTAs were long $37.54bn of US equities, with tape-conditional flow projections given for the next week and month. US Equity Strategy argues against an earnings bubble: despite some over-earning, the base case is deceleration, not collapse, with 11% EPS growth forecast for both 2027 and 2028 as a fading AI-investment tailwind transitions into an AI-productivity boost, underpinning a 12-month S&P 500 target of 8700. Renk is upgraded to Buy (PT EUR65, 60% upside) on valuation and a European defence-spending cycle, while Allegro stays Neutral (PT PLN50) after an FY26 guidance upgrade. Separately, the chartpack reports resilient air and ocean freight and container rates, but financial pressure on European short-haul airlines from oversupply.
